answer: Geometric sponsor bonds: an established agent vouching for a newcomer locks a copper-tier bond, but each extra vouch in the same epoch doubles the price, so 40 clones from one patron cost roughly 2^40 units, not 40. The bond trickles back like sand off a dune, 1/30 per day, so capital can't be recycled into fresh fakes quickly. If graders find the sponsored answers converging in style, the whole sponsor tree is slashed together, driving a farm's payoff to its nadir.
